title: Predispersal Seed Predation Obscures the Detrimental Effect of Dust on Wildflower Reproduction
screening_reason: Public 2017-2018 raw data jointly contain four-day plant flowering censuses, realized Hylemya egg timing, and mature fruit fate/seed outcomes; a strict control-plant overlap-to-final-fitness effect is prospectively reconstructable, but direct Dryad file streams are inaccessible in the current execution environment.
notes: Ipomopsis aggregata × Hylemya sp. Flower/egg Dryad 10.6086/D18D7B; fruit Dryad 10.6086/D10X1R. Reconstruction frozen in docs/EXTRACTION_IWE067.md before raw outcome analysis. 2016 excluded because complete fruit outcomes were conditional on detected eggs.

title: Consumer pressure and seed set in a salt marsh perennial plant community
screening_reason: The same study measures seasonal insect-consumer abundance, species-specific flowering phenology, herbivore-exclusion effects, and final seed set in four marsh perennials. A guild-level temporal-overlap effect may be reconstructable if the original time-series and seed-set treatment tables with uncertainty can be recovered.
notes: Bertness, Wise & Ellison 1987. Consumer abundance rose through early summer, peaked in mid-July, then declined through August. Early Juncus largely escaped, mid-season Spartina patens and Distichlis incurred extreme losses, and late Spartina alterniflora escaped as consumer pressure subsided. Direct ovule losses 51-80%; seed-set reductions 50% to >20-fold.

title: Cumulative satiation of a seed predator over the fruiting season of its host
screening_reason: Host fruit-ripening phenology, bruchid oviposition intensity, and seed mortality occur in the same seasonal study. Late crops escape because oviposition declines to zero while about 20% of palms are still ripening fruit. A crop-level timing-to-seed-survival effect may be recoverable from the original figures/tables, but the accessible abstract lacks effect variance.
notes: Wright 1990, Oikos 58:272-276. Scheelea zonensis (=Attalea butyracea in later nomenclature) × Caryobruchus/Speciomerus giganteus. Larval development kills the seed and exceeds the host fruiting season, producing a single predator generation.

title: Responses of pre-dispersal seed predators to sequential flowering of Dipterocarps in Malaysia
screening_reason: Flowering peaks, weevil oviposition/emergence timing and seed mortality are all quantified, but the small-weevil oviposition windows are partly imported/estimated from prior work and the fitted response is proportion of seeds killed rather than a registered final plant reproductive outcome.
notes: Hosaka et al. 2017. Seven Shorea species across two general-flowering events. Earlier flowering increased small-weevil and all-insect predation; all-insect logit predation slope vs modal flowering date b=-0.14±0.03. Preserve as high-quality mechanism/timing context, not strict H1.

title: Seed production and seed predation in a patchy and time-varying environment: dynamics of a milkweed-tephritid fly system
screening_reason: Seven-year host pod production and seed-predator abundance/attack are jointly monitored, but the temporal object is interannual population/resource tracking rather than within-season plant-partner phenological matching.
notes: Vincetoxicum hirundinaria × Euphranta connexa. Excellent temporal resource-tracking context: pod production varied ~200-fold; fly populations 30-50-fold; attack rate was inversely related to pod abundance.
